settlements.decision: The UI package (sutra_app.ui) is the only server of HTML pages and static files. GET / is Home. GET /d/{dept}/ is the J2 page; GET /d/{dept} answers 308 to the slash form with the query kept. GET /?dept=<id>[&other] answers 308 (Cache-Control: no-store) to /d/<id>/[?other] as a compatibility shim only (no section generates that link form any more; an invalid or unknown dept is ignored and Home is served). The engine serves no page: no pages.py, no GET / or /vendor/ route, no sutra_dept cookie, no default department. engine.md already says this (4.9; 7.1 rows 1-2; ENG-D4 'no cookie, no hidden default department'; its module map has no pages.py): the stale statements are in ui.md 0, 3.2 and 13 and in sections.json. paths.ui_dir() is NOT created, so there is nothing for it to return: tests that need the UI files import sutra_app.ui.PAGES_DIR, and the engine's legacy J2 flow tests read J2's own page, harness and vendor folder through SUTRA_J2_CHECKOUT (they skip with a printed reason when it is unset). The engine's stdlib adapter j2_server.py is for legacy tests and a single-run dev server only: it serves HERE/j2_ui.html only when HERE is set, never imports sutra_app.ui, and python -m sutra_app never starts it.
settlements.why: ui.md owns the 12 page edits and the boot block that carries the write token, so the UI package must render both pages. engine.md has already given up GET / and the cookie. A cookie is shared by every tab and every port of 127.0.0.1 (RFC 6265 section 8.5; measured in Chrome 156, see S3-web-03), so two departments in two tabs, or two app instances, would collide; a path cannot. One owner per page.

settlements.topic: The write token: header or cookie, the Origin check, where it is enforced (task 3)
settlements.decision: The token travels in the header X-Sutra-Token ONLY. No cookie exists anywhere (no sutra_token, no sutra_dept). Rule, by method: every request whose method is not GET, HEAD or OPTIONS needs the header with the per-launch token (secrets.token_urlsafe(24), compared with hmac.compare_digest, never written to disk) else 401 bad_token; if an Origin header is present it must equal 'http://' + the Host header value, otherwise (including Origin: null from a sandboxed frame) 403 bad_origin; an absent Origin is allowed (curl, httpx, TestClient); reads and EventSource carry no token. Host check: TrustedHostMiddleware(['127.0.0.1','localhost']) on the whole app (pages, static files, SSE, plug-in routers) answers 400 bad_host. The token and Origin checks live in ONE dependency, require_token, in sutra_app/orchestrator/api/deps.py, exposed as Services.require_token; the engine's routes use Depends(services.require_token) and the connectors' router receives it as write_guard, which becomes a REQUIRED keyword argument (no None default). The name write_guard exists only as that parameter name. Safety net: a route-walk test fails when any route in app.routes (plug-ins included) whose methods are not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS lacks Services.require_token in its dependency tree, or when a plain Starlette route or Mount accepts a non-GET method. The browser gets the token from the boot JSON block (render_page), sutra_ctx.js sends the header on every non-GET: J2's five POSTs through the fetch wrapper, orchestrator calls through api.post.
settlements.why: A cookie is not isolated by port (RFC 6265 section 8.5), and I measured it in Chrome 156 with two servers on 127.0.0.1 ports A and B: B received A's cookie, and after B's response set its own, the next request to A carried B's value. The app picks the next free port from 8780 to 8799, so a second instance would overwrite the first one's token and give it 401s. A cookie also rides along on every same-origin request, including those of a generated page; a header does not. The boot block is already per instance. One path means one test matrix. The dependency form was verified by the orchestrator (FastAPI 0.162) and is already what the engine and connectors call; the route-walk test removes the one risk of that form (a forgotten Depends).
settlements.rejected: Either header or cookie (ORCH-D9 as written: two paths, the cookie path rests on SameSite alone); cookie only; token in the URL; a middleware as the second enforcement point; a separate name write_guard for a second dependency.

settlements.topic: SSE: event names, ids, payloads, Last-Event-ID replay, polling fallback (task 5)
settlements.decision: The 11 event names of orchestrator 6.3 and the UI's TYPES agree one to one (server.hello, server.resync, chat.turn, chat.message, chart.changed, chart.approval, graph.updated, task.updated, atom.updated, usage.recorded, needs_you.changed) and so do their payloads (UI examples match 6.3). Changes: (1) add the connector router's three events, published through the same EventBus: connector.health {provider, state, until, reason}, connector.switch {session_id, from, to, reason}, connector.mode {mode}; the UI's TYPES gets them (14 names) and Home's Settings pane refetches GET /api/health on any of them. The library's node.state is not an SSE event: node changes travel in graph.updated. (2) Ids: the id: line is the integer seq, process-local, starting at 1 each launch; server.hello and server.resync are control events and carry NO id: line, so the browser's lastEventId always names a real event. (3) Replay: Last-Event-ID or ?after=n; if n is greater than the head (the id comes from a previous launch) the server sends server.resync {reason:'restart'} and then the live tail; if n is older than the 1000-event ring, server.resync {reason:'gap'}; else it replays n+1 to head. server.hello is always first. (4) Client rule: within one connect() handle the first server.hello is ignored (the page has just loaded everything); every later server.hello (browser auto-reconnect or the manual re-create after a hard close) is handled exactly like server.resync: refetch everything shown. This also covers id collisions across launches. A manual reconnect creates a new EventSource without ?after=. (5) Polling fallback after three errors, every 2 s, no token: GET /api/graph (compare version), GET /api/chart (version) and /api/chart/changes?after=<last seq>, GET /api/needs-you, GET /api/departments (Home rail), GET /api/chats/{sid}/messages?after=<last id> for each session on screen, GET /api/graph/nodes/{id} while #nodepanel is open; it stops when a hello arrives. (6) The ping is an SSE comment every 15 s; JavaScript cannot see comments, so no client watchdog is designed. topics= filters by the prefix before the dot (connector is a topic).
settlements.why: Names and payloads already match; what was open is the restart case (ids restart at 1 each launch, so an old Last-Event-ID can collide with a new id), the missing connector events that the connector section publishes, and an incomplete polling list (the Home rail and the change log would freeze). Refetch-on-hello is a client rule only and needs no protocol change.
settlements.rejected: An epoch inside the id (custom id parsing for no gain once hello triggers a refetch); persisting seq across launches; a JS heartbeat watchdog (comments are invisible to EventSource); WebSocket.

settlements.topic: J2's stdlib server compares POST paths exactly (task 6)
settlements.decision: Confirmed in the J2 source (ce2631f): do_GET parses with urlparse(self.path).path, but do_POST compares self.path with ==, e.g. self.path == '/api/say' (j2_server.py:250-263), so a POST with a query string (?dept=x) falls through to 404 '{}'. This matters only when the ported page, whose fetch wrapper appends ?dept=<id> to every J2 call when SutraCtx.dept is non-empty, is served by a stdlib server. The app never does that: python -m sutra_app runs uvicorn on the FastAPI app, the UI router serves the pages, and the FastAPI routes take the query (ENG 7.2). J2's own unported page has dept empty, so the wrapper adds nothing and J2's own server keeps working. For robustness the vendored adapter (engine/j2_server.py) routes POST by urlparse(self.path).path, like GET, and a test pins it.
settlements.why: Two ways the stdlib server could meet the ported page: a developer starts it by hand, or a legacy test points the ported page at it. Costs one line and removes the trap; J2's file itself is never touched.
settlements.rejected: Patching J2's j2_server.py (J2 stays untouched); serving the ported page from the stdlib adapter; stripping the query in the browser wrapper (it would break the FastAPI scope rules).

settlements.topic: Wire words the UI must adopt from the orchestrator: ids, statuses, edge kinds, atom state, chat POST errors (found while comparing payloads)
settlements.decision: The UI conforms to the orchestrator's wire; nothing is renamed on the server except where S3-web-04 and S3-web-15 say. (a) Ids are LIB/ORCH ids: root 'root'; chart nodes their chart id (a department 'web'); function nodes '<dept>.<fn>' ('web.identity'; the final spec writes '<department_id>/<kind>' but the id is a URL segment of /api/graph/nodes/{id}, so the dot of library 8.1 stays); steps 's-' + 10 hex; sessions 'cs_org' and 'cs_' + 12 hex; tasks 'tsk_' + 12 hex; changes 'chg-NNNN'; requests 'req-<n>'. The UI treats every id as opaque text and validates the department of /d/{dept}/ with the generic URL-id rule ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,120}$ and then Services.department; the strict department rule (^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$, no underscore) stays with the orchestrator's bad_id check. The UI's n:, f:, s: prefixes and org_<12 hex> ids leave code, fixtures and examples (orchestrator open item U-1 closed). (b) Node status = J2 map words plus archived: idle running waiting waiting_on_you fault filed done_unchecked left_open not_made archived. GraphRender.statusLook is keyed by them; the UI's older words (working, queued, blocked, failed, done, done_open) are deleted; an unknown word is drawn as idle and counted in warnings. (c) Edge kinds: structural contains, has_function, has_step build the tree; cross links handoff (amber, solid), depends_on (blue; with label 'revises' terracotta), speaks_to (blue, dotted, label = message count), step and any unknown (blue). The UI's 'feeds' and 'rework' kinds are deleted. A dashed loop is drawn only for a reverse twin of the SAME kind. Projector rule: a step-to-step relation is stored once, as depends_on from the reading step to the step it reads (from reads[] and rework); the engine's handoff[] on a step event is the inverse of reads[] (engine 4.5) and is NOT stored, because it would draw every pair twice as a false loop; handoff edges are function-to-function (along the spec's routes) and function-to-builder. (d) Atoms: the lifecycle field on the wire is 'state' (open, closed, verify_failed, abandoned; 'refused' never leaves the API); the UI's fixtures change 'status' to 'state'; FnodeView.normalize reads state and falls back to status; goal, attempt, ts_open, ts_closed, task_id, node_id, schema stay top-level; work kind, verify template, closed_by and reason are read from body. (e) Chat POST errors: on cs_org the preflight answers 503 provider_unavailable or cli_missing and stores nothing, so the composer keeps its text and shows error.message with a link to Settings; a failure inside a turn answers 202 first and then marks the message state 'error' with a Retry button. On department, division and J2 /api/say posts there is no preflight and no 503: a missing CLI shows as the run's system line and run.ended crashed (engine F7 b). (f) Bootstrap row: the chart log's first row is actor 'system'.
settlements.why: orchestrator 1.3 (U-1) and library 18.2 already chose the ids and the status words and ui.md 0 says 'the UI conforms'; the UI examples were written against an earlier orchestrator draft. Edges: the false-loop problem is real because the engine publishes both directions of each dependency. Chat errors: the UI's X1 assumes 202 always, orchestrator T0 answers 503 before storing; and J2's page ignores non-2xx answers of /api/say, so a 503 there would vanish silently.
settlements.rejected: Server-side n:/f:/s: prefixes; translating at the API edge; keeping both status vocabularies; storing both handoff and depends_on for one relation; an id with a slash for function nodes; a 503 on department posts.

settlements.topic: Generated content is served sandboxed so it cannot read the page token (found while checking task 3)
settlements.decision: Every engine response whose content type is text/html (GET /site/{key} with and without ?run=, GET /api/artifact for html, markdown-rendered documents) carries Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups; frame-ancestors 'self'. Every engine response carries X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. This is added once, in sutra_app/engine/api/reply.py (to_response). The two preview iframes of the J2 page also get sandbox='allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups' in the markup (edit E2) as a second layer; the artifact iframes already use sandbox=''. create_app sets docs_url=None and redoc_url=None (they load their JavaScript from a CDN, so they are broken offline, D6); /openapi.json stays. Consequence accepted: a generated site that uses localStorage, cookies or fetches the app's own API fails inside the preview; the site is a static deliverable and J2's own checks run it outside the app. Measured here with Chrome 156: without the header a same-origin framed page read the parent's boot token ('parent-readable:SECRET-TOKEN-123'); with 'sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups; frame-ancestors self' the framed script still ran but reading the parent threw SecurityError.
settlements.why: The token sits in a JavaScript-readable boot block and the generated website is model-written HTML served from the same origin, so without a sandbox any script in a generated site could read the token and post to the chat agent, which can run model CLIs. ui.md R10 left 'the framed generated site is governed by its own response headers (server section)' and no section defines them. This is also the reason the header token (S3-web-03) is safe and a cookie would not be.
settlements.rejected: Serving generated content from a second port or origin (a second server); allow-same-origin in the sandbox (defeats it); an iframe attribute only (a new-tab open would be unprotected); stripping scripts from generated sites.

settlements.topic: Error envelope, library route names and the J2 path list (found while comparing routes)
settlements.decision: Three small route-space rules. (1) Every NEW route (orchestrator, library API, connectors API) answers errors with the orchestrator's envelope {error: {code, message, details}}; the connector section's flat {error: code, kind: kind, detail: message} becomes {error: {code, message, details: {kind}}}. The engine's J2-compatible routes keep J2's own bodies (text 'not found', {error: 'no such run'}, {ok: false}) because the J2 page reads them; the only ORCH-shaped errors there are 401/403 from the guard and 403 read_only. (2) The Interface library's read-only router moves from /api/library/schemas... to /api/schemas, /api/schemas/{family}/{version} and POST /api/schemas/validate, because /api/library already means J2's template library (ENG 7.1 rows 10-11, the Library tab) and the UI's J2 path list treats the /api/library/ prefix as J2's. (3) J2_PATHS in sutra_ctx.js matches whole pathnames exactly (/api/state, /api/runs, /api/call, /api/preview, /api/docs, /api/map, /api/plan, /api/library, /api/run-templates, /api/artifacts, /api/artifacts/tree, /api/artifact, /api/agent, /api/code, /api/story, /api/board, /api/audits, /api/refs, /api/say, /api/output, /api/reset, /api/playbooks/clear, /api/lessons/clear) except four prefixes: /api/library/, /site/, /file/, /shot/; so the orchestrator's /api/runs/{run_id} never gets a dept parameter.
settlements.why: The UI's ApiError reads one envelope; two shapes on new routes would need two parsers. The prefix match on /api/runs would add dept to /api/runs/{run_id}, and /api/library/schemas would be handled as J2's template library. All three are cheap now and expensive after code exists.
settlements.rejected: One envelope for the J2 routes too (breaks the unchanged J2 page); keeping /api/library/schemas; prefix matching for every J2 path.
